metadata.title: Supplement 2: National Adaptations of International Context Questionnaires (PIRLS 2016 User Guide for the International Database)
metadata.venue: TIMSS & PIRLS (Lynch School of Education, International Study Center)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS 2016 user guide supplement describing how countries adapted PIRLS 2016 context questionnaire items for inclusion in the international database. It does not provide an analytic sample, scaling, or any instructions for applying student/school weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT, TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the supplement is not an empirical analysis paper, there is no weighting strategy to extract; users should consult the main PIRLS 2016 technical documentation for sampling design and weight variables when conducting secondary analyses. For secondary analyses, the key implication of this supplement is that some questionnaire variables may be marked Code D (comparable) or Code X (not included), which affects which background variables can be used with appropriate comparability assumptions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This supplement does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes or generate/transform Plausible Values (PVs). Instead, it documents questionnaire item adaptations and whether country data are included in the international database (Code D) or excluded (Code X). Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to an empirical modeling context because no statistical estimation or imputation procedure is performed in this document.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level analytic sample is defined. The supplement lists questionnaire items and, for each country (and some subnational benchmarking locations), indicates whether the national adaptation is included in the international database (Code D) or excluded (Code X). Therefore, there is no filtering criterion for an analytic dataset beyond the Code D/Code X inclusion rule for secondary use of background variables.

data.outcome_summary: This document is not an empirical study; it is a PIRLS 2016 user-guide supplement that catalogs national adaptations to PIRLS 2016 context questionnaires (Student, Home/Learning to Read, Teacher, and School). For each adapted background question, it reports the question stem/response options, the variable name(s), and the national adaptation by country, assigning Code D when the national data are considered comparable to the international version and Code X when the country’s data are not included in the international database (e.g., not administered, not applicable, or deleted for comparability/data-quality reasons). It also includes subnational “benchmarking participants” entries (e.g., cities/regions) where applicable. Because no modeling, PV scaling, or statistical estimation is performed, there are no performance metrics or causal/predictive effects to report; the primary “result” is guidance for selecting which background variables are valid for secondary analyses using PIRLS 2016 international data.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse because the provided text is a questionnaire adaptation guide rather than an empirical paper. There is no dependent variable, no ML model training/evaluation, no reported sample size, and no PV or missing-data handling procedure—only documentation of which questionnaire items are comparable (Code D) versus excluded (Code X). As a result, fields such as total_students, per-country n_students, and main findings are not applicable to this document’s purpose.
